source.note: Unofficial transcript aligned to the owner-supplied recording. Teachers should treat wording as a review aid, not an ETS-issued script.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Do you know when the next train is? I need to be at the Museum of Fine Arts by 10:30.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Actually there is a shuttle bus at 10 that takes you directly there. And it’s only a 25-minute ride.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: It was such a great weekend. I saw two really good movies on the play. What did you do?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: What you were supposed to be doing? Studying! Did you forget we have an exam today?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: So what are they supposed to be building over there? Another gym?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Isn’t that where the new library is going?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Do you mind if I use your computer to write a history paper? Mine’s out for repairs.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Sorry, I am in the middle of typing something and it’s gonna be a while. You know, the computer lab is still open.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Hi Gina, that’s a really cool watch. Where did you get it?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well, my sister works at the jewelry store right off campus.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Do you think classes are gonna be canceled because of the snow storm?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I sure hope so. It says on the radio that the roads are treacherous. Why don’t you check with the administration office?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: So where is Gloria these days? It likes that she is disappeared.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: You obviously haven’t been to the library in a while.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I don’t know what you did to this computer. But it keeps giving me these error messages.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Oh, sorry, I was playing around with it before you came in. Let me take a look at it.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Chicken or fish? I know they are both good here. But I just can’t make up my mind.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Come on. We haven’t got all night.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Oh no, I just remembered I was supposed to give Tom his CD back when I see him in class today. But I left it sitting on the kitchen table.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I don’t think it’s any big deal. I am sure he can do without it until our next class.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I’m starting to lose my voice, which usually lose I am about catch a cold. Do you think I should go to the clinic and have my throat looked at?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: As soon as possible, esp. since we have four exams next week in German class.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Are you sure you want to rent that apartment? It is the first one you saw.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: You’re right. I shouldn’t be so hasty. It wouldn’t hurt to check out a few more.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Wow, you are really tall. Are you in a basketball team?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I may be tall but that doesn’t mean I’ve ever been any good as a player.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Which of these shirts do you think I should buy? The red or the green one?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well, didn’t you already buy a red one last week? A little variety would be good.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I was surprised to hear that you’ll accept the job offer from the bank. Are you sure you’ll like working there?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well, I just thought I would give it a try. If I don’t like it, I can quit any time.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I’m having a party tonight. Can you make it?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I’d love to, but my aunt’s here only one day. And I promised to take her to a play.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: How are you gonna pay for classes next year? Did you apply for financial aid?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well, I am working at a bookstore and doing some tutoring. That should be enough. Don’t you think?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Excuse me. I didn’t order this cake.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: It comes with your dinner, Ma’am.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: You know something? I can’t wait to go home for spring break. My hometown is so small that everybody knows you.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Yeah, and everybody knows your business, too. And talks about it all the time.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: You did a great job, coordinating the student volunteers for the campus open house fell. I hope we can count on you again.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I’m glad things worked out. But this is it for me. It is too time-consuming.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: What time should Peter have been here to meet us?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: As soon as his psychology class was finished. I hope he didn’t forget.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I missed the meeting about on-campus job openings this afternoon. Were you there?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I don’t have time for a job this semester, but my roommate went. And I can get you copies of the forms you need from her.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: One thing I definitely recommend: make sure you get enough sleep the night before your presentation. Trust me. It will make difference.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I don’t know, professor. That won’t be easy. Probably I will lie awake all night, rehearsing my talk.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Do you think we will have a say on what musical our theatre group will be presenting next year?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: I doubt it. I heard the director say she’d already picked one out.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Hi, Jim. I hear you are looking for an apartment closer to work.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Yes, I am sick and tired of spending so much time in my car.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I’ve got great news. Ben’s going to be senior class president next year.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: They’ve had the elections already?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Someone said we really should go to that guest lecture tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Well, it wasn’t me. I couldn’t care less about astronomy.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Trust me. You don’t want to go to that movie. It’s not nearly as good as the reviews said.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: I don’t care. I need a break form studying. And it’s the only thing showing that I haven’t already seen.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: If this dry weather keeps up, we are going to be restricted again in how we used water this summer.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Unless we really start doing something about it now.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Hi, Mike. I heard that you were revising the instructor’s manual for the computer class. Is there anyway I could get a copy of the new version?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Well, I’m still working on it. So for right now everyone should just use the one they have.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Hi, Ed. Looks like you were here early.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Yeah. Class doesn't start for a ten more minutes, so I put up the novel I’m reading.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: What is it?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: It is called Sister Carrie. It is about a woman named Carrie who leaves her country home to earn a living in Chicago and New York.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Oh, I've studied Theodore Dreiser. His work is a little depressing, but I like him, even though his characters always get in trouble. He tricks them with sympathy. How do you like Sister Carrie?

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: It's not what I expected. On the back cover it says the book created a lot of controversy when it was first published in 1900. It even says the publisher withdrew out from market after only 500 copies were sold. But I don't see why.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well. The novel might not be shocking by our standards but it sure created a stir then. Think about what Carrie does. She leaves her country home and gets caught up in some personal scandals in the city. Now most other authors of that time would have punished the character to provide a moral lesson, but Dreiser has Carrie become a successful actress at the end.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Wow, that puts the story in a different perspective. I bet Dreiser must have been discouraged when the publisher took it off from market.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: He sure was. He stopped writing fictions for a while and did work as a journalist and an editor.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Well, how did the book become recognized?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Some British reviewers praised the novel and then another publisher released it in 1907. Eventually people recognized the novel for its realism and Dreiser went on to write other successful works.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Before we began today's topic, I'd like to review the phases of child language acquisition that we went over yesterday. Who'd like to summarize for us? Yes, Lisa.

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well, first of all, you said that new-borns only make rudimentary vocalizations because the voice box isn't in position for speech yet. But that at about three month of age baby starts to utter the first sounds that resemble language sounds. The sounds of consonants like "k" and "g".

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: That's right. And after this stage come the meaningless syllables, a consonant followed by a vowel. For example, the "dada" sounds. And at the next stage comes a real breakthrough. Can you tell us about that, Lisa?

segments.speaker: Woman
segments.text: Well, between six months and one year of age, babies begin to associate sounds with meaning. So, when you say "dog", they know you're referring to the four-legged animal that is their house pet. At this stage they start to build a vocabulary. And in a matter of month they are learning ten to twenty new words a day. This vocabulary growth continues until adolescents.

segments.speaker: Man
segments.text: Right. And isn’t it amazing that by the time children are two or three years old they are stringing sentences together? Certainly no one would dispute that children had a tremendous capacity for learning language, what linguists are still trying to determine is how this language acquisition takes place.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: How did the native communities of the southeastern Canada convey information to one another? In general, they used couriers memorized oral messages. Among some peoples, the Iroquois and the Algonquians for example, messengers also used code based on strings of beads. The beads were called "wampum" and the color of the beads signified the message. For instance, white beads were used for news of peace, prosperity, or good will. Purple beads meant war, disaster or death. The couriers also carried messages for early European explorers and missionaries. One jazz missionary described in his journals how a courier memorized 20 different detailed transactions, delivered them to Montreal and then returned with exact what price to each. He had traveled 800 miles round trip. Sometimes the messages were written, not oral and will be passed from one courier to another. When one messenger arrived to the edge of his tribe's territory, he would sell the letter to the next messenger, usually at a profit. If the letter passed through many hands before reaching the receiving end, the final bill could be very expensive.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: We've talked before about using special plantings, water, and feeders to attract birds to your garden. This afternoon I'd like to tell you about a less well-known way to attract birds. It's by putting out eggshells. Many birds eagerly consume them. Perhaps it is a method of replacing calcium lost by females and egg-laying, though I have seen males eat the shells too. Anyway, I have had at least eight different species of birds come to eat the eggshells. Here is how it's done. You should save your eggshells and rinse them in water, then cook them lightly on the baking pan in the oven; set at a low temperature until they are dry but not brown. This sterilizes them and makes them brittle. You can crumble them into bite-sized pieces and spread them on the ground, a rock, or a bird feeder. You may find them so popular you want to go to your favorite restaurant to ask for more eggshells.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Last week when we talked about landslides, we looked at what causes these huge masses of earth to move down the natural incline such as a mountainside or slope with such destructive force. Now when these landslides occur in populated areas, what can humans do to avoid or minimize damage? Basically there are three things that can be done. The first thing is to simply avoid construction in the areas where landslides are likely to happen. Typically when a side on the slope is chosen for new construction, it is important that a geological survey of the area be conducted. The survey reveals unsafe conditions such as too little vegetation or soil that would absorb water too easily, conditions that might lead to a landslide, say, during periods of heavy rains. The second thing is to build in a way that doesn't make stable slopes unstable. For example, natural vegetation, like grass, is needed to keep soil firmly in place. This vegetation should not be entirely removed since without the grass the soil would loosen up and this could result in a landslide. The third thing is to design good water drainage to ensure that the water naturally runs down the slope and doesn't build up in the soil. This kind of water buildup on the slope is one of the most frequent causes of landslides. Water buildup can easily result during long periods of heavy rain and sometimes the cause is part of the construction itself such as a stonewall that blocks the water from draining off the slope.
